name: Hiel
title: The Rebuilder of Jericho
summary: Hiel from Bethel was a man who rebuilt Jericho during the reign of King Ahab. By doing so, he fulfilled Joshua's curse, and it cost the lives of his eldest son Abiram and his youngest son Segub. His fate serves as a warning about the consequences of defying God's word.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's Curse over Jericho
keyEvents.description: When Joshua conquered and destroyed Jericho, he pronounced a curse on anyone who would rebuild the city: they would lose their firstborn at its foundation and their youngest at the setting up of its gates.

keyEvents.title: The Rebuilding of Jericho
keyEvents.description: Hiel from Bethel rebuilt Jericho during the reign of King Ahab, in defiance of Joshua's curse. This occurred in a time marked by apostasy and disobedience to God in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Abiram
keyEvents.description: When Hiel laid the foundation of Jericho, he lost his eldest son Abiram, exactly as Joshua had prophesied several hundred years earlier.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Segub
keyEvents.description: When Hiel rebuilt the gates of Jericho, he lost his youngest son, Segub. In this way, Joshua's prophetic curse was completely fulfilled.

keyEvents.title: A Warning in Ahab's Time
keyEvents.description: Hiel's fate is set against the backdrop of Ahab's wickedness and apostasy, illustrating how God's word always comes to pass, even after many generations. Ahab's reign was marked by idolatry and contempt for the Lord's word.
